newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: U.N. war crimes body arrests ex-Vukovar president.
newsitem.headline: U.N. war crimes body arrests ex-Vukovar president.

text.p: The U.N. war crimes tribunal said on Friday it had arrested a Serb ex-mayor of Vukovar under whose control one of the former Yugoslavia's first exercises in ethnic cleansing was carried out.

"Slavko Dokmanovic was arrested on 27 June 1997 by ICTY (International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia) investigators in Eastern Slavonia...He was then transferred to The Netherlands," the tribunal said in a statement.
It said Slavko Dokmanovic was President of Vukovar Municipality in November 1991, when the JNA (Yugoslav People's Army) and Serb paramilitaries abducted around 260 men from the city's hospital.
"(The men) were later transported in groups to a site close to Ovcara where they were shot and killed," the statement said, adding 200 bodies were recovered from the site in 1996 by forensic experts.

Dokmanovic was indicted on March 26 last year by the tribunal in an amendment to the so-called "Vukovar indictment" earlier issued against three JNA officers charged with involvement in the alleged massacre.

The prosecution alleges that 260 non-Serb men sheltering in Vukovar hospital were rounded up and slaughtered by JNA forces in a systematic orgy of violence which later became the blueprint for "ethnic cleansing" in the former Yugoslavia.
Dokmanovic was being held at the tribunal's detention cells in Scheveningen near The Hague, the tribunal said.
